title: calibration of advertised C_q vs empirical violation rate

host.uname: Darwin <redacted-host> 25.5.0 Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0: Tue Jun  9 22:26:15 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.121.10~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 arm64

config.violation_def: PRIMARY (demand-based): sum of class-rounded sizes of the fill's written pages (exact, via telemetry-ring drains every 4096 successful writes) > budget, or HARD_FAILURES delta > 0 — exactly the event P(sum > B) <= 1-q that C_q bounds
config.violation_ladder_def: SECONDARY: VIOLATIONS delta > 0 or HARD_FAILURES delta > 0 during fill; saturates ~1 for all q because the advertisement targets B_total while R3 fires at 0.97*B_total (ladder/advertisement interaction, reported as such)
config.demand_measurement_assumption: tier telemetry records class-rounded size once per successful write only; ring_capacity=4096 and this contract is the sole writer
config.overflow_def: demand_overflow = max(0, demand_bytes - budget); overflow_bytes = max(0, peak PHYS_USED during fill - 0.95*pool_bytes) (spec'd; ~0 whenever the ladder works)

data.note: Primary 'violation' is demand-based (realized fill bytes > advertised budget) — the exact event C_q bounds; 'violation_ladder' additionally reports the R3/hard-failure definition, which saturates near 1 for every q because the advertisement targets B_total while the R3 watermark sits at 0.97*B_total (see config.violation_ladder_def). With 60 seeds per cell the resolvable violation probability is coarse: at q=0.99 the target rate 0.01 cannot be distinguished from 0 with 60 Bernoulli trials (Wilson 95% CI for 0/60 spans up to ~0.060). Violation magnitude (overflow bytes) is reported alongside to strengthen the calibration story.
